headline: THE SPEEDUP IS REAL, EVERY TIMING FIGURE REPRODUCES, ALL EIGHT OF MY MUTATIONS OF A CLAIMED PROPERTY DIE, AND THE ITEM STILL FAILS ON ITS OWN LOAD-BEARING CRITERION. The batched lint narrows py_compile's exception surface from `Exception` to three named families, and two classes escape: a RecursionError from a long expression chain (reached at 19,997 bytes) and a MemoryError from the parser stack (a 20,000 term ternary chain, or a 20,000 term string concatenation). MEASURED against the loop it replaced, on the same tree: the loop names both poisoned files AND the genuine SyntaxError that sorts after them, prints `lint: FAIL`, exits 1. The new stage dies on the first one with a traceback that names NO path, prints NO `   FAIL:` line, prints NO summary line, and leaves EVERY REMAINING FILE UNCHECKED. That refutes AC2's `every failure is still named by path on its own line', it is first-error-wins for those classes (the property the five-defect probe claimed closed, measured only with SyntaxErrors), and it is the `checks FEWER files than before' failure mode the spec's own risk paragraph exists to prevent. Exit status is still non-zero so the gate goes RED and no false GREEN exists, which is why this is a defect and not an incident. The fix is one word: py_compile catches `Exception' at /usr/lib/python3.12/py_compile.py:68, and I proved the same interpreter RECOVERS from both classes and keeps naming subsequent failures correctly. Everything else about this item is in good shape, and I say that having tried hard to break it.
must_fix_before_live: B1 THE BATCHED LINT ABORTS INSTEAD OF NAMING THE FILE ON TWO ERROR CLASSES THE PER-FILE LOOP HANDLED, AND THE REST OF THE CORPUS THEN GOES UNCHECKED. scripts/check_lint.sh:81 catches `(SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError)`. py_compile.compile wraps source_to_code in `except Exception as err` (/usr/lib/python3.12/py_compile.py:68) and py_compile.main maps both PyCompileError and OSError to a non-zero exit, so under the loop EVERY Exception raised by compilation was a named per-file failure. MEASURED, fifteen error classes run through both stages side by side in throwaway git repositories: thirteen agree exactly (invalid syntax, IndentationError, TabError, a null byte, a bad coding cookie, a UTF-8 BOM, invalid UTF-8, CRLF, an empty file, a tracked directory, a broken symlink, a mode-000 file, an 18 MB valid file). TWO DIVERGE. RecursionError: `x = 1' followed by 9,996 `+1' terms, 19,997 bytes, is the smallest case; a 20,000 term string concatenation across lines, an ordinary generated-file shape, also reaches it. MemoryError: a 20,000 term `1 if 1 else' chain overflows the parser stack. In both, the old loop printed `Sorry: RecursionError: ...' then `   FAIL: aaa_recursion.py', then went on and ALSO named `zzz_broken.py' and `zzz_broken.sh', and printed `lint: FAIL'. The new stage printed a four-frame traceback naming `File "<stdin>", line 76, in <module>' and NOTHING ELSE: no path, no FAIL line, no summary, and zzz_broken.py never checked. THIS ALSO REFUTES THREE SHIPPED SENTENCES that make checkable claims: scripts/check_lint.sh:15 (`every failure is still named by path on its own line'), scripts/check_lint.sh:71 to 76 (`THE THREE NAMED FAILURES are the three ways a file the loop handed to py_compile could make it exit non-zero' and `the stage carries on to the next file exactly as the loop did'), and proof/WARP-0711/manifest.json:57 (`THREE EXCEPTION FAMILIES ARE HANDLED and each was exercised', which presents the three as exhaustive). THE FIX IS AT THE PREDICATE, not a new fixture: catch `Exception`, which is exactly what py_compile catches, so the stage mirrors the loop instead of enumerating the exceptions someone thought of. I PROVED IT RECOVERS: with `except Exception` in one interpreter over poison_recursion.py, poison_memory.py, after_ok.py, after_broken.py, poison_recursion2.py, after_ok2.py in that order, all three failures are named, both valid files pass, and the two poison files do not poison their neighbours. THE MISSING TOOTH: the fixture set at scripts/selftest.py:20577 contains only shapes inside the three families, which is why 3192 assertions pass over a stage that stops checking. Add a fixture whose compilation raises OUTSIDE the three families and assert BOTH that it gets its own `   FAIL: <path>` line AND that a broken fixture sorting after it is still named, so the assertion tests continuation and not only detection.

B2 `EXACTLY ONE STAGE FAILED' DOES NOT REPRODUCE AT THE REVIEWED COMMIT, AND THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT IS NOT ESTABLISHED FOR THE SHIPPED STATE. proof/WARP-0711/manifest.json:45 and :115 state that verify.sh in the hostile worktree `ends GATE: RED ... and EXACTLY ONE stage failed - lint - while unit (3173 passed / 0 failed), generated, docs, extra, secret scan, contracts and the shape gate all passed, so the red is attributable to the lint failure alone'. I planted the same six defects (five broken python, one broken shell) in a detached worktree AT cfb8cc7 and ran the gate to completion: GATE: RED, exit 1, wall 195.32s, and THREE stages failed, not one. lint FAIL, naming all six on their own `   FAIL:` lines with `lint: FAIL (699 python, 173 shell, 0.82s)`, which reproduces the manifest exactly. unit FAIL at 3188 passed / 4 failed, TWO of the four being this item's OWN assertions (`WARP-0711 AC2 NO BYTECODE OVER THE REAL CORPUS, race-free' and `WARP-0711 AC3: over THIS repository the stage exits 0'), both of which require the live corpus to lint clean, plus WARP-1102's two footprint dogfood assertions. shape gate FAIL, six `the diff touches ... outside the footprint' problems. The manifest's own `unit (3173 passed / 0 failed)' figure shows the experiment ran at 7df08a1, in a tree that does not contain this item's assertions, so the sentence is scoped but its conclusion about attributability is not established for the commit under review. PROVED OR DELETED: restate it as what was measured in that tree, and add what the same experiment does at cf20743, or delete the attributability claim. The gate does still attribute the cause, because the six paths are named on the lint stage's own lines, so this is a record defect and not a code defect.

notes: N1 THE SIGPIPE RESTORATION HAS ZERO TEETH, AND IT IS THE ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE IN THE STAGE WITH NO ASSERTION BEHIND IT. Mutation m7 replaced scripts/check_lint.sh:48 (`signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_DFL)`) with a no-op and ran the whole suite in its own detached worktree: 3192 passed, 0 failed. I THEN PROVED THE CLAIM TRUE MYSELF, which is why this is a note and not a finding: over a 6,000 broken file corpus, so the output exceeds the pipe buffer and a real SIGPIPE is delivered, the writer's status is 141 for BOTH stages under `| head -1`, under `| true` and under a read-one reader, and 0 for both over an all-passing corpus, so the assumption at manifest.json:159 that this RESTORES the old behaviour is exactly right. Two further pipe shapes: stdout to /dev/null keeps exit 1 on a real failure in both stages, and stdout to /dev/full gives 120 for the new stage against 1 for the old, both non-zero, so a full disk cannot mask a failure and turns a pass into a false RED rather than a false GREEN. THE GATE'S OWN CAPTURE CANNOT MASK ANYTHING: scripts/verify.sh runs the stage as `if bash -c "$cmd"` with stdout inherited and consumes only the exit status; it never pipes and never captures. Against this item's own standard (`each of it asserted rather than claimed'), the SIGPIPE sentence should be asserted or deleted.

N2 THE DOGFOOD ASSERTION PINS THE SPEC DEFECT THE SAME MANIFEST ASKS SOMEONE TO CORRECT. scripts/selftest.py:20753 asserts `_L07_FM.get("placement") == ["engine"]`, so the gate turns RED the day a legitimate correction to `placement: [enforcement]` lands. The builder declares this at manifest.json:156 and the declaration is honest, and any assertion that RECORDS a live defect necessarily dies when the defect is fixed, so this is not the WARP-1210 class of an accidental pin. It is still avoidable: the finding is the RELATIONSHIP, that no footprint glob of this spec resolves to `engine` and the area therefore comes from the placement declaration alone, and that can be asserted without the literal. I verified the relationship myself: arch.area_for_path('plugin/templates/scripts/check_lint.sh') is the empty set, arch.area_for_path('scripts/check_lint.sh') is {'enforcement'}, and only the declared placement supplies `engine`.

N3 THE LOAD-BEARING EQUALITY WOULD GO FALSE-RED ON A TRACKED PATH THAT IS NOT A REGULAR FILE. The recording shim at scripts/selftest.py:20540 records an argument only when `[ -f "$a" ]` holds. I confirmed `-f` is FALSE for a dangling symlink and FALSE for a directory, so a tracked submodule path or a tracked dangling symlink ending in .py or .sh would be listed by the new stage and NOT recorded by the loop shim, making _L07_NEW_SET minus _L07_LOOP_SET non-empty on a tree that is not actually unequal. It fails CLOSED, so it can only cost a false red and never mask a real inequality, and this repository tracks no such path today (I walked all 866 and every one is a regular file). Worth widening the shim to `-e` plus a symlink test the day a submodule appears.

N4 NEITHER STAGE HANDLES A TRACKED PATH CONTAINING A SPACE, AND THE EQUALITY ASSERTION PASSES ONLY BECAUSE THE DEFECT IS SYMMETRIC. The loop word-split `$(git ls-files '*.py')` and the new stage calls `out.split()`, so `a b.py` becomes two tokens in both, the real file is never compiled in either, and both name two nonexistent fragments as failures. Faithfully preserved, out of this item's scope, and no such path is tracked. Recorded because AC2's `the SAME file set' is true here in the sense of bug-for-bug identical rather than correct.

N5 A FAVOURABLE DIVERGENCE THE DIFFERENTIAL DOES NOT COVER, RECORDED SO THE RECORD IS COMPLETE RATHER THAN ONLY UNFAVOURABLE. On a READ-ONLY checkout with every file valid, the old loop reports `[Errno 13] Permission denied: '__pycache__'   FAIL: <path>' for EVERY python file and exits 1, because py_compile's .pyc write fails; the new stage prints `lint: pass' and exits 0. The new stage therefore deletes a whole spurious failure class. The manifest's `IDENTICAL failing sets' claim is correctly scoped to the eight-fixture repository so it is not overstated, but this improvement is unrecorded and is a second reason the bytecode change is a win.

N6 THE FOOTPRINT DECLARES TWO GLOBS FOR PATHS THAT HAVE NEVER EXISTED IN ANY REVISION. `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format='' -- '*check_lint.sh'` returns exactly one path, scripts/check_lint.sh. specs/WARP-0711-lint-one-interpreter.md:25 and :26 should go with the AC3 correction; they are what makes the AC3 clause look buildable when it is not.

N7 HOUSEKEEPING NOT THIS ITEM'S BUT VISIBLE FROM IT: /tmp/gateprof, the `git clone --shared' the 2026-07-25 baseline session used and names at proof/WARP-0711/baseline.md:4, is still on disk. It is a clone rather than a worktree so `git worktree list' does not show it. This build's own three worktrees are gone as claimed.

residual_rulings.DECLARED SPEC DEFECT (a) - AC3's engine-: LEGITIMATE SPEC DEFECT, and the substitute is an HONEST RESTATEMENT rather than a weakening. I ruled it by attack on all four load-bearing facts rather than by reading the argument. (1) THE PATHS DO NOT EXIST AND NEVER HAVE: `git log --all --diff-filter=A --name-only --format='' -- '*check_lint.sh'` returns exactly scripts/check_lint.sh across the whole history, and nothing named check_lint.sh exists under plugin/ or packs/ on disk. (2) THE ENGINE MANIFEST DOES NOT COVER THE PATH, which I read rather than took: PK.ENGINE_GLOBS is scripts/verify.sh, scripts/warp-guard.sh, scripts/*.py, scripts/runners/**/*, bin/warp, .warp/*.py, .warp/*.yaml, .github/workflows/warp-gate.yml, specs/TEMPLATE.md, plans/TEMPLATE.md. It names two .sh files individually and has no glob over scripts/*.sh, so a scripts/check_lint.sh in plugin/templates would be an engine file by nobody's definition and the drift check could not hold it identical. That is a stronger statement than the builder's synthetic-engine experiment, and it agrees with it. (3) WIRING WOULD NEED A FORBIDDEN CHANGE: plugin/templates/scripts/verify.sh:17 is `CHECK_lint="na:no linter adopted yet"`, that file is one of the 7 PROTECTED paths in .warp/policy.yaml, and the spec's Out of scope forbids any change to verify.sh. So the letter of AC3 is reachable only by creating seven dead ungoverned copies or by breaking the spec's own boundary. (4) THE WARP-0623 PRECEDENT SAYS WHAT IS CLAIMED, verbatim: proof/WARP-0623/manifest.json:132 records `AC5 asks for ... BYTE-IDENTICAL across plugin/templates and every pack. That is not satisfiable as worded and was not done', with the same repo-only substitute, and proof/WARP-0623/manifest.json:121 records that its own independent reviewer `ruled the resolution HONEST and THE SPEC WRONG to demand it'. NOT A WEAKENING: what AC3's clause protects is that adopters run the same enforcement, and the engine ships NO lint stage at all, so there is nothing to keep in sync. The substitute proves more than a byte comparison over seven absent files could: exactly one tracked copy, none under the canonical engine or any declared pack_dir, pack drift empty across all 7 packs, and the globs demonstrated not to cover the path. THE OWNER MUST STILL CLOSE THE SPEC: either delete the clause and the two dead footprint globs, or open a separate item to PROMOTE the stage into the engine, which is a different footprint and an owner decision about giving adopters a lint stage they have not declared.
residual_rulings.DECLARED SPEC DEFECT (b) - the risk sent: REAL SPEC DEFECT, correctly diagnosed, and ACCEPTABLE to leave to the owner for this round. MEASURED myself against .warp/architecture.yaml: arch.footprint_areas is {'engine', 'enforcement'}, arch.footprint_tier_floor is 'high', arch.placement_gate is empty, arch.area_for_path('scripts/check_lint.sh') is {'enforcement'}, and arch.area_for_path('plugin/templates/scripts/check_lint.sh') is the EMPTY SET. So `engine' enters from `placement: [engine]` at specs/WARP-0711-lint-one-interpreter.md:22 and from no file at all, and the risk sentence's stated reason at :7 to :9, `a gate stage plus its seven engine copies', is FALSE: there are no engine copies and there never were. I also measured the counterfactual the builder asserts without running it: with `placement: [enforcement]` the areas collapse to {'enforcement'} and the tier floor is EMPTY, so the declared `high' would be an explicit owner judgement rather than a derived floor. Two further facts I add. First, arch.placement_gate returns empty in BOTH configurations, so the wrong placement is invisible to the gate and would have shipped unnoticed if the builder had not looked. Second, removing only the two dead footprint globs does NOT change the outcome, because the crossing comes from the placement, which confirms the diagnosis is at the right level. ACCEPTABLE UNCORRECTED BECAUSE: the tier is right either way, no protected path is involved, the build instruction permitted only the status line, and the discrepancy is recorded in the gate rather than in prose. See N2 for the one thing I would change about how it is recorded.
residual_rulings.DECLARED SPEC DEFECT (c) - the corpus co: NOT A DEFECT THAT MUST BE FIXED BY CHANGING THE NUMBER, and I would refuse a change that did. AC1's checkable claim is about what the BASELINE ARTIFACT records, and proof/WARP-0711/baseline.md:121 records 662 Python and 172 shell correctly for its 2026-07-25 measurement, so AC1 is satisfied as written and the assertion that reads those two substrings is reading a FROZEN historical record rather than a live property. The title at specs/WARP-0711-lint-one-interpreter.md:4 is DATED rather than wrong in kind, and it sits in a spec whose own Context says `Why the seconds are not the criterion: the machine varies. The attribution ... does not', which puts corpus size in the same category. THE HONEST CORRECTION IS TO DATE THE FIGURE, not to renumber it: renumbering makes the title a moving-property pin written in prose, which is the defect class the owner's freshest lesson names, and it would go stale again on the next commit. Minor spec hygiene, non-blocking, and the delta was published by the builder rather than left for me.

disposition: DO NOT LAND YET, AND THE FIX IS SMALL. This is a good item that measured its own cost honestly, published the two figures that did NOT reproduce before a reviewer could find them, declared its own shipped-for-one-commit resolver defect with the red gate figure attached, named three spec defects instead of quietly working around them, and wrote 19 assertions that killed all eight of my mutations of a property it claims. The speedup is real and reproduces on my clock at 17.3x, the file-set equality is the right load-bearing choice and is proven by executing the old stage rather than re-deriving it, and nothing outside the stage moved. It fails on one thing, and it is the thing the whole item is for: the batched stage stops enforcing on an input class the per-file loop handled, and a lint that stops checking after file N of 694 without naming a path is worse than a slow one. CHANGE `except (SyntaxError, ValueError, OSError)` AT scripts/check_lint.sh:81 TO `except Exception`, which is what py_compile catches and therefore restores the contract rather than widening it; add a fixture outside the three families with a broken fixture sorting after it, so the tooth proves CONTINUATION and not only detection; correct the two manifest sentences that made the three families sound exhaustive and the one that says exactly one stage failed. Then this lands. The three spec defects are the owner's to close and none of them blocks: (a) legitimate, substitute honest, WARP-0623 precedent verified; (b) real, correctly diagnosed, acceptable to leave; (c) dated rather than wrong, and the honest fix is to date the figure and never to renumber it.
